ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the perpendicular bisectors of line segments $AB$ and $BC$, denoted as $ {l}_{1}$ and $ {l}_{2}$, intersect at point $O$. If $\angle 1=40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line BO and extend BO to point P, \\
$\because$ the perpendicular bisectors $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ of line segments AB and BC intersect at point O, and $l_{1}$, $l_{2}$ intersect AB, BC at points D, E respectively, \\
$\therefore$ AO=OB=OC, $\angle$BDO=$\angle$BEO=$90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DOE + $\angle$ABC=$180^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle$DOE + $\angle$1=$180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABC=$\angle$1=$40^\circ$, \\
$\because$ OA=OB=OC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$A=$\angle$ABO, $\angle$OBC=$\angle$C, \\
$\because$ $\angle$AOP=$\angle$A+$\angle$ABO, $\angle$COP=$\angle$C+$\angle$OBC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOC=$\angle$AOP+$\angle$COP=$\angle$A+$\angle$ABC+$\angle$C=2$\angle$ABC=2$\times$40$^\circ$=$\boxed{80^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is triangle ABC, B and C are on the same straight line below, and A is at the upper right. Two straight lines l1 and l2 intersect at point O; l1 is the perpendicular bisector of segment AB, and l2 is the perpendicular bisector of segment BC. The marked ∠1 in the figure is the angle between l1 and l2, given as 40°. Reasoning: Because l1 ⟂ AB and l2 ⟂ BC, the angle between straight lines AB and BC is equal to the angle between straight lines l1 and l2, therefore ∠ABC = ∠1 = 40°. Also because O lies on the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC, OA = OB and OB = OC, thus OA = OB = OC, and O is the circumcenter of triangle ABC. Therefore ∠AOC is the central angle subtended by chord AC, and ∠ABC is the inscribed angle subtended by the same chord AC. The central angle is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle subtending the same arc, so ∠AOC = 2∠ABC = 2 × 40° = 80°.
